title: Remove Duplication from Playbooks
objective: Replace distribution-specific duplication with portable modules, variables, and lists.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting Started with Ansible 08 - Improving your Playbook
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A working playbook can still be expensive to maintain. Repeated tasks drift apart when a package name, state, or option changes in only one copy.

The generic package module selects the host’s package backend, and variables isolate values that truly differ. A list or loop expresses repeated resources without repeating the surrounding task structure.
Refactoring should preserve outcomes. Preview the revised play, run it, and compare the final state before deleting the original implementation.
explanation.rule: Abstract repeated mechanics, but keep meaningful platform differences visible.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
- name: Install baseline tools
  ansible.builtin.package:
    name:
      - curl
      - git
    state: present
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Why prefer ansible.builtin.package when the operation is portable?
options: It selects the platform package backend

feedback.correct: Correct—this matches the demonstrated workflow and keeps the automation explicit.
feedback.incorrect: Review the rule of thumb and the relevant video checkpoint before continuing.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Replace distribution-specific duplication with portable modules, variables, and lists.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

lab.title: Refactor safely
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Run the original package tasks in check mode.
Replace them with the portable list-based task.
Run twice and require changed=0 on the second execution.
lab.success: Both tools are present and the repeated run is unchanged.
